headline: My Citizenship Status Has Been Downgraded to 'Pending' Because I Forgot My Grade 4 Geometry Certificate
body:
I didn't think twice when the desk officer asked for my 'foundational proof of existence' during my routine residency verification. I handed over my Aadhaar, my passport, and a utility bill, but he just sighed and asked for the exact physical compass box I used in the fourth standard to prove I learned the concept of circles in this specific geographical territory. Apparently, without that rusted protractor, my entire history as a citizen is legally circular, and therefore, non-existent.

He told me I was currently in 'documentation purgatory' until I could produce a signed affidavit from my 1998 class teacher attesting that I didn't cheat on my geometry final. I tried to explain that the school was demolished in 2012 to make way for a luxury mall, but he just pointed to a stack of files labeled 'Incomplete Provenance.' Now, I spend my lunch hours scouring Facebook for classmates who might still have their old geometry sets, hoping that their preserved sets might serve as a proxy for my own citizenship.

It’s gotten so bad that I’ve started carrying a makeshift geometry kit everywhere, just in case I get stopped by a roving inspector. If I can prove that I know how to draw a perfect equilateral triangle right there on the sidewalk, maybe the state will finally acknowledge that I’m a real person again. In the meantime, I’ve been advised to avoid leaving my pincode, as the 'territorial integrity' of my status is reportedly far too fragile to survive a transit through a state border.
caption: Living proof that your childhood geometry homework is the only thing keeping you from being legally invisible. 📐📜 #BureaucracyLife #PaperworkHell #CitizenshipStruggles #IndiaNews (satire)

It avoids the repetitive 'chatbot/digital portal' trope that plagued several other submissions, making it feel fresh and uniquely funny while maintaining a clean, deadpan structure.
